summary: Three of the four exact-pinned dependencies have published advisories: lodash 4.17.15, requests 2.19.0 and Flask 3.0.3. dayjs 1.11.13 has none. Neither manifest has a lockfile, so the pinned manifest versions were queried.

findings.title: lodash 4.17.15 has multiple known vulnerabilities
findings.evidence: "lodash": "4.17.15". OSV returned 6 advisories. The worst are command injection (GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm, CVSS 3.1 base 7.2) and code injection via _.template (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVSS 3.1 base 8.1). The others are prototype pollution (GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw, GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg) and ReDoS (GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9).
findings.recommendation: Upgrade lodash to 4.18.0. That is the lowest fixed version that covers all six advisories. 4.17.21 fixes only some of them.

findings.title: requests 2.19.0 has multiple known vulnerabilities
findings.evidence: requests==2.19.0. OSV returned 11 advisories. The worst is credential exposure on an https-to-http redirect (GHSA-x84v-xcm2-53pg / PYSEC-2018-28, CVSS 3.1 base 7.5). The others include a .netrc credential leak, a Proxy-Authorization header leak, verify=False session reuse, and insecure temp file reuse.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade requests to 2.33.0 or later. That is the highest of the fixed versions and covers every advisory returned.

findings.title: Flask 3.0.3 session missing Vary: Cookie header
findings.evidence: Flask==3.0.3. GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726 / PYSEC-2026-2151: the session does not add a Vary: Cookie header in some access paths. The CVSS v3 vector (PYSEC-2026-2151) gives a base score of 4.3. The CVSS v4 vector on GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726 is low, but the worst advisory sets the rating.

limitations: express ("*", package.json line 7) and gunicorn (unpinned, requirements.txt line 3) have no exact version, so they were not queried. The dependency_hygiene step covers them.
No lockfiles exist, so transitive dependencies were not examined.
